newsitem.title: USA: Biogen says Q1 Avonex sales top $52 mln.
newsitem.headline: Biogen says Q1 Avonex sales top $52 mln.

text.p: Biogen Inc Chief Executive Officer Jim Tobin said Thursday first quarter sales of the Cambridge, Mass.-based pharmaceutical company's multiple sclerosis drug Avonex were $52.6 million, 18 percent higher than the previous quarter.

Analysts, including Oppenheimer & Co Inc's Matt Geller, had expected strong sales of Avonex, a treatment for relapsing forms of MS, to hit $50.4 million in sales. Oppenheimer has the company rated outperform.
"That $52.6 million is not way beyond the consensus, but it is on the high side," Tobin said.
Biogen, which lost German patent rights to Avonex in a decision announced Wednesday, will still market the drug in Germany, the U.K., Sweden, Finland, Israel and Cyprus.

"What it did (the German court's ruling) was remove from my armament of weapons one potential weapon to extract royalties from Schering (Schering-Plough Corp) or Sorono (Laboratories, Inc) or anybody else," Tobin said.

Tobin, pleased with Avonex sales, noted several other products were in the pipeline. CVT-124, a treatment for congestive heart failure, and LFA3TIP, a treatment for severe psoriasis sufferers, entered stage II clinical trials this week, he said.
The company's CD40 Ligand, billed as a treatment for lupus and other autoimmune diseases, has begun phase I clinical trials, Tobin said.

And the company was able to license Hirulog, a heart drug that remains the subject of a shareholder lawsuit, to a start-up company called The Medicines Company. Under the March licensing agreement Tobin said Biogen received a small payment, but "the real value of the out-licensing agreement would be if it makes it to market, there are substantial royalties involved."
Overall, Biogen reported a net income for first quarter of 1997 of $17.01 million or $0.22 per share. First Call said the consensus of 20 analysts who follow the company was also $0.22 cents a share.
